title: Homily I — Received into heaven with songs

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily I on the Dormition, cols. 716-717 (PDF leaves 399-400)

source_text: Σὲ συνεπόρθμευσαν σὺν ἀρχαγγέλοις ἄγγελοι. Σοῦ τὴν ἔξοδον ἔφριξαν τὰ ἀκάθαρτα καὶ ἐναέρια πνεύματα. Σοῦ τῇ διαβάσει εὐλογεῖται μὲν ἀὴρ, αἰθὴρ δὲ καθαγιάζεται. Σοῦ τὴν ψυχὴν χαίρων οὐρανὸς ὑποδέχεται. Σοὶ μεθ' ἱερῶν ὕμνων καὶ φαιδρᾶς τελετῆς προσυπαντῶσι δυνάμεις, μονονουχὶ λέγουσαι· τίς αὕτη ἡ ἀναβαίνουσα λελευκανθισμένη, ἐγκύπτουσα ὡσεὶ ὄρθρος; καλὴ ὡς σελήνη, ἐκλεκτὴ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος. Ὡς ὡραιώθης, ὡς ἡδύνθης! σὺ ἄνθος τοῦ πεδίου, ὡς κρίνον ἐν μέσῳ ἀκανθῶν· διὰ τοῦτο νεάνιδες ἠγάπησάν σε. Εἰς ὀσμὴν μύρων σου δραμούμεθα. Εἰσήνεγκέ σε ὁ βασιλεὺς εἰς τὸ ταμεῖον αὐτοῦ, ἔνθα ἐξουσίαι δορυφοροῦσιν, ἀρχαὶ εὐλογοῦσι, θρόνοι ἀνυμνοῦσι, τὰ Χερουβὶμ ἐκπλήττεται χαίροντα, δοξάζει τὰ Σεραφὶμ τὴν τοῦ οἰκείου δεσπότου φύσει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ οἰκονομίᾳ χρηματίσασαν μητέρα. Οὐ γὰρ ὡς ὁ Ἠλίας ὡς εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐλήλυθας· οὐχ ὡς ὁ Παῦλος ἕως τρίτου διεβιβάσθης οὐρανοῦ· ἀλλ' ἕως αὐτοῦ τοῦ βασιλικοῦ θρόνου τοῦ Υἱοῦ σου ἔφθασας, αὐτόπτως ὁρῶσα, καὶ χαίρουσα, καὶ σὺν πολλῇ καὶ ἀφάτῳ τῇ παῤῥησίᾳ παρεστῶσα, ἀγγέλοις θυμηδία ἀπόῤῥητος, καὶ πάσαις ταῖς ὑπερκοσμίοις δυνάμεσι, πατριάρχαις εὐφροσύνη ἄληκτος, δικαίοις χαρὰ ἀνεκλάλητος, προφήταις διηνεκὴς ἀγαλλίασις, κόσμον εὐλογοῦσα, τὰ σύμπαντα ἁγιάζουσα, τοῖς κάμνουσιν ἄνεσις, τοῖς πενθοῦσι παράκλησις, τοῖς νοσοῦσιν ἴασις, τοῖς χειμαζομένοις λιμὴν, ἁμαρτάνουσιν ἄφεσις, τοῖς λυπουμένοις εὐμενὲς παραμύθιον, πᾶσι τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν ἑτοίμη βοήθεια.
pass_a_gloss: You angels with archangels ferried across together. At your exodus (ἔξοδος) the unclean (ἀκάθαρτα) and aerial (ἐναέρια) spirits shuddered. By your crossing (διάβασις) air (ἀήρ) is blessed, and ether (αἰθήρ) is hallowed (καθαγιάζεται). Your soul heaven rejoicing receives. To you with holy hymns and bright rite/festival (φαιδρὰ τελετή) powers (δυνάμεις) come to meet, all but (μονονουχί) saying: Who is this coming up whitened (λελευκανθισμένη), peeping forth as dawn (ὄρθρος), beautiful as the moon, choice (ἐκλεκτή) as the sun? How you were made beautiful, how you were made sweet! You flower (ἄνθος) of the plain, as a lily (κρίνον) in the middle of thorns; for this reason young women (νεάνιδες) loved you. Into the scent of your ointments (μύρα) we will run. The king brought you into his storeroom/chamber (ταμεῖον), where authorities (ἐξουσίαι) act as bodyguard, principalities (ἀρχαί) bless, thrones (θρόνοι) hymn, the Cherubim are astounded rejoicing, the Seraphim glorify the one named (χρηματίσασαν) mother of their own master by nature (φύσει) and truth (ἀληθείᾳ), by economy (οἰκονομίᾳ). For not as Elijah as into heaven have you gone; not as Paul were you carried across up to a third heaven; but up to the very royal throne of your Son you arrived, seeing with your own eyes (αὐτόπτως), and rejoicing, and standing by (παρεστῶσα) with much and unspeakable (ἄφατος) freedom of speech (παρρησία), to angels an unutterable delight, and to all the supercosmic (ὑπερκόσμιοι) powers, to patriarchs unceasing gladness (εὐφροσύνη), to righteous ones unspeakable joy, to prophets continual exultation (ἀγαλλίασις), blessing the world, hallowing all things, to the toiling relief (ἄνεσις), to the mourning comfort (παράκλησις), to the sick healing (ἴασις), to the storm-tossed harbour (λιμήν), to sinners release (ἄφεσις), to the grieving a kindly consolation, to all who ask ready help (βοήθεια).
pass_b_english: Angels, with archangels, carried you across. The unclean spirits of the air shuddered at your going forth. At your passing the air is blessed and the upper air is made holy. Heaven receives your soul with joy. The Powers come out to meet you with holy hymns and a radiant festival, all but saying: “Who is this who comes up in white bloom (Song of Songs 8:5), looking forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, chosen as the sun (Song of Songs 6:10)? How beautiful you have become, how sweet (Song of Songs 7:6)! You are the flower of the field, like a lily among thorns (Song of Songs 2:1-2); therefore the maidens have loved you. We will run after the fragrance of your perfumes. The king has brought you into his chamber (Song of Songs 1:3-4).” There Authorities stand guard, Principalities bless, Thrones sing praise; the Cherubim are struck with joyful wonder, and the Seraphim glorify her who, by nature and in truth, in God's saving plan, became the mother of their own Master.

For you have not gone, like Elijah, “as it were into heaven” (2 Kings 2:11); you were not carried, like Paul, as far as the third heaven (2 Corinthians 12:2). But you have reached the very royal throne of your Son, seeing him with your own eyes, rejoicing, and standing beside him with great and untold boldness: an unspeakable delight to the angels and to all the powers above the world, unceasing gladness to the patriarchs, joy beyond words to the righteous, lasting exultation to the prophets. You bless the world and sanctify all things. You are rest for the weary, comfort for those who mourn, healing for the sick, a harbour for the storm-tossed, forgiveness for sinners, kindly consolation for the grieving, ready help for all who ask.

choices.note: Song of Songs citations follow English numbering: 8:5 'who is this coming up' with the LXX 'whitened' (λελευκανθισμένη, 'in white bloom'), which English Bibles from the Hebrew render 'leaning on her beloved'; 6:10 (margin 'LXX 6:9'); 7:6; 2:1-2 (the Song's first person 'I am the flower' turned to 'you are'); 1:3-4 ('therefore the maidens love you', 'we will run', 'the king has brought me into his chambers', turned to 'you').

'As it were into heaven' keeps the printed doubled ὡς (ὡς ὁ Ἠλίας ὡς εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν), which quotes the LXX of 2 Kings 2:11 (4 Kingdoms 2:11), 'as it were into heaven'; not in the margin, cited as a clear quotation.
The ranks of Powers, Authorities, Principalities and Thrones may recall Colossians 1:16 and Ephesians 1:21; not a quotation, uncited.
'Spirits of the air' may recall Ephesians 2:2; uncertain, uncited.
παρρησία rendered 'boldness' (freedom to speak before God).
Edition note (15): Reg. reads 'with bright lamps' (καὶ φαιδραῖς ταῖς λαμπάσι) for 'and a radiant festival' (καὶ φαιδρᾶς τελετῆς);
